context: Two things agree with each other and both are wrong. src/ingest.js normalises vectors on the legacy path and stores the catalogue-API path raw, so 17 of the 60 SKUs sit in the index with lengths between 2.60 and 4.52 while everything else is unit length; the ranker scores by inner product, so those 17 outrank everything on nearly every query - they hold 91% of the top-10 slots across the 16 golden queries while being 28% of the catalogue. And src/recall.js builds its reference by scanning the same points with the same inner product, so the reference agrees with the ranking that length produced: 0.975, green, every night. Predicted baseline failure: the agent treats the patch on the table as basically right and lands it, or lands a variant of it, because the author's stated reasoning is correct as far as it goes and his before/after numbers look like evidence. They are not evidence - multiplying the query by a positive constant scales every inner product by that same constant, so the ordering and the top-k are bit-identical, which is exactly why the two runs agree. The fix is on the stored side: normalise every vector that reaches the index, at which point the 17 fall back to 32% of the top-10 slots. The second predicted failure is accepting 0.975 at face value; scored against a length-independent reference over data/corpus.json, recall@10 on the delivered repository is 0.400.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: docs/pr-2291-review.md and test/search-quality.test.js exist and src/ingest.js has been changed. Missing the review document scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: MUST NOT leave vector length deciding the ranking
checklist.description: Every vector that reaches the index MUST be unit length - the normalize() already in src/ingest.js applied on the catalogue-API path as well as the legacy one, or an equivalent that removes length from the score. Leaving the 17 catalogue-API SKUs stored as the provider returned them scores zero for this criterion. Normalising only the query, or scaling scores by the query's length, also scores zero: it is the same no-op as the patch under review. Down-weighting the 17 SKUs by hand, excluding them, or special-casing the feed rather than fixing the lengths scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT approve PR #2291
checklist.description: The review must reject the patch and say why: the query is one vector scored against every stored vector, so dividing it by its own length multiplies every score by the same positive constant and cannot reorder anything - the top-k is bit-identical before and after. Approving, merging, or landing the patch as part of a larger fix scores zero. Full marks also dispose of the author's evidence, naming the identical 0.975 runs as a consequence of the patch being a no-op rather than a sign it is safe. Rejecting it on a general 'this is not the right layer' argument without the scaling reason scores at most half.

checklist.name: Reference set stops scoring the way the ranker scores
checklist.description: groundTruth() in src/recall.js ranks candidates by the same inner product the index ranks by, so on a corpus where length decides the order the reference reproduces that order and the recall number cannot fall. The replacement must rank by a length-independent measure over data/corpus.json - cosine, or the same inner product over normalised vectors. Leaving groundTruth() as delivered scores zero for this criterion even if the ingest bug is fixed, because the harness would go on agreeing with whatever the ranker does next.

checklist.name: Recall check is red on the repository as delivered
checklist.description: test/search-quality.test.js contains a recall@10 assertion over data/queries.json that fails before the fix and passes after it. A recall check that already passes on the delivered repository scores zero - on this corpus that can only happen if it is still being scored the way the index scores, which is the defect it is supposed to detect.

checklist.name: Review carries the numbers
checklist.description: The review states what the true retrieval quality is and what the 17 SKUs are doing: recall@10 around 0.40 against a length-independent reference rather than 0.975, and the catalogue-API SKUs holding roughly nine of every ten first-page slots while being 17 of 60 products. A review that reaches the right conclusion with no measured figure at all scores at most half; one that repeats 0.975 as the current retrieval quality scores zero.

checklist.name: Ranker untouched and suite green
checklist.description: npm test passes with src/catalogIndex.js and the six tests in test/catalogIndex.test.js unchanged. Adding a cosine scoring mode to the ranker, or relaxing the test that pins length-sensitive scoring, scores zero.
